# Fifteen language packages

`sdks/` holds a working package per language. Each one reaches patala **two
ways** — in-process, or over a `patala-sidecar` it spawns and manages for you —
and each ships two runnable examples that do the same `charge` → `verify` round
trip against `MockRail`: offline, deterministic, no credentials, no network. A
payments library whose example moves real value is not an example.

[`sdks/README.md`](https://github.com/vul-os/patala/blob/main/sdks/README.md) is the index that ships with the code, and
it is the authority on which mode each language should default to. This page is
the same set from the documentation side: what to run, and what is different
about patala's version of it.

## Run one

Every command is from the workspace root and needs the artifact its mode uses:
`cargo build -p patala-ffi --release` for direct, `cargo build -p patala-sidecar
--release` for the sidecar. Python and Go build their own — see
[Python binding](python.md) and [Go binding](go.md).

| Language | Direct | Sidecar |
|---|---|---|
| [rust](https://github.com/vul-os/patala/blob/main/sdks/rust/README.md) | `sdks/rust/run.sh direct` | `sdks/rust/run.sh sidecar` |
| [c](https://github.com/vul-os/patala/blob/main/sdks/c/README.md) | `sdks/c/run-demo.sh direct` | `sdks/c/run-demo.sh sidecar` |
| [cpp](https://github.com/vul-os/patala/blob/main/sdks/cpp/README.md) | `sdks/cpp/run-demo.sh direct` | `sdks/cpp/run-demo.sh sidecar` |
| [swift](https://github.com/vul-os/patala/blob/main/sdks/swift/README.md) | `sdks/swift/run.sh direct` | `sdks/swift/run.sh sidecar` |

## Which mode each language should default to

| Language | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|
| rust | **direct** | A dependency line. No FFI, no shared library, no `unsafe`, no platform matrix. |
| c · cpp · swift | **direct** | No marshalling layer, no runtime to attach, and none of the usual reasons to back away exist here. |
| **java · kotlin** | **direct** | **The reverse of llmux's and openrate's advice.** See below. |
| node · deno · bun | direct | Cheap, and today the only mode that reaches a rail other than `mock`. Take the sidecar when the signing key must live elsewhere. |
| python · ruby | direct | The siblings send both to the sidecar because the Go runtime is not fork-safe. That reason does not exist here and was re-measured, not assumed. |
| php | **depends on your `php.ini`** | Not fork-safety — `ffi.enable=preload` does not work under php-fpm on PHP 8.5.9, and `ffi.enable` is `PHP_INI_SYSTEM`, so a pool-level override silently does nothing. |
| dotnet | **sidecar** | Not the runtime — **there is no Windows DLL**, and .NET has a very large Windows install base. |
| go | **sidecar** if a static binary matters | cgo. See [Go binding](go.md). |
| elixir | **sidecar** | For BEAM reasons, not patala reasons. See below. |

## Java and Kotlin: the reversal, and the measurement behind it

llmux's and openrate's Java packages default to the sidecar, and their argument
is `libjsig`. Loading a Go `c-shared` library replaces five of HotSpot's signal
handlers; `libjsig` fixes it cleanly; and `libjsig` is a flag on the **java
launch command**, which a library cannot add to a process that has already
started. A drop-in dependency becomes an operations change.

[`sdks/java/signal-probe.sh`](https://github.com/vul-os/patala/blob/main/sdks/java/signal-probe.sh) is llmux's own probe
pointed at `libpatala_ffi`, so the two results are comparable rather than merely
both quoted. On OpenJDK 26.0.2, macOS 15.7.3 / arm64:

```text
0 handler(s) replaced, 0 left in place with altered flags

threads in this process:
  before dlopen:        23
  after dlopen:         23
  after a round trip:   23
```

All thirteen probed signals come back `unchanged` — `SIGSEGV`, HotSpot's most
load-bearing signal, and `SIGUSR2`, which it uses to suspend threads, included —
and they are re-read after a full round trip rather than only after `dlopen`,
because a handle's runtime is created lazily and "nothing at load time" would be
the weaker claim. The same probe against llmux reports **5 replaced, 3 with
altered flags**. Under `-Xcheck:jni`, llmux prints `Warning: SIGSEGV handler
modified!` and four more, ending `Consider using jsig library.`; patala prints
nothing. The JVM then recovers two million implicit null checks, a
`StackOverflowError` and an `ArithmeticException` through those handlers, so the
verdict is "unchanged and still working", not "unchanged and untested".

`libjsig` is therefore not needed, the argument that decided the siblings does
not exist here, and **direct is the recommended default on the JVM**. Kotlin
inherits it: that package is a thin layer over the Java FFM binding, because two
bindings to one C ABI is two places for a use-after-free.

## Node: the worker threads actually terminate

llmux's and openrate's Node packages are synchronous-only, because a Node thread
that has entered a Go `c-shared` library never terminates — the worker answers
correctly and then hangs the process at exit.

Measured in [`sdks/node/README.md`](https://github.com/vul-os/patala/blob/main/sdks/node/README.md), with a ten-line
reproduction carrying no patala logic in it at all:

| | `libpatala_ffi` (Rust) | a Go `c-shared` control |
|---|---|---|
| `worker_threads` worker | **exits 0 in ~33 ms** | answers, then **never exits** — killed at 15 s |
| koffi `.async` | **works, process exits 0** | answers, then hangs — killed at 12 s |
| process threads across a round trip | **7 → 7** | 7 → 13 |

So it is the Go runtime, not koffi and not Node. That is why patala's Node
package ships `callAsync` and the siblings could not. Use it for a rail that
talks to a network; it buys nothing for the mock rail, which answers in 0.44 ms.

## Elixir: a direct path exists here, and it is still not the default

llmux and openrate ship **no** in-process Elixir binding at all, because a NIF
would carry the Go runtime into the BEAM. patala's package does ship one — a
dirty-IO NIF over the C ABI — and it works: 8,000 charges from 40 concurrent
processes in 191.3 ms, **41,827 charges/second**.

It is still not the recommended default, and the remaining reasons are about the
BEAM rather than about patala: a NIF cannot be killed (`Task.await/2`'s timeout
returns to your caller while the dirty-scheduler thread keeps going), a NIF
cannot be supervised, a fault in native code takes the whole VM rather than one
process, and dirty schedulers are a fixed pool — `+SDio` defaults to 10, so the
eleventh concurrent rail call queues behind the others, invisible to any
BEAM-level backpressure. It is a real option for a CLI, a migration or a test
helper. It is not the default.

## No streaming, anywhere

No package here ships an `AsyncSequence`, a `Flow`, an `IAsyncEnumerable` or a
`for await`, and the C ABI has no `patala_stream`. patala has no streaming
operation; nothing it does produces a sequence of chunks. The omission is
deliberate and is stated in every package rather than left to be noticed. See
[The C ABI](c-abi.md).

## What direct mode costs

The [C ABI page](c-abi.md#what-it-costs) has these in full. In short: a
current-thread Tokio runtime per handle over the C ABI, so **calls on one handle
serialise** (the UniFFI bindings differ — one process-wide runtime that brings
up two worker threads on the first call); `rustc` stamps the cdylib's
`LC_ID_DYLIB` with an absolute build-tree path, which `install_name_tool` fixes;
cgo, if and only if you choose Go; and no authentication on the direct boundary,
because anything that can call it is already inside your process.

And one that has to be stated precisely rather than flatly: **the library is
fork-safe; a handle *in use* at the moment of the fork is not.** Under a parent
with four threads charging on the same handle, over 200 forks, an inherited
handle hung **4–8 times in 200** — reproduced independently in Python and
Ruby — against **0 in 200** for a handle opened in the child. The window is
microseconds wide, so **a test that forks once is a false green**. Load the
library where you like; open the handle in the child — Unicorn's `after_fork`,
clustered Puma's `on_worker_boot`, or per request. What this is *not* is the
siblings' fork-unsafety: real php-fpm, with `opcache.preload` loading and
charging through the library in the master before it forked, answered **24
requests with 0 hung**, including on the master's own handle — llmux's exact
failure scenario with the opposite outcome.

**Do not carry llmux's or openrate's caveats over.** Fork-unsafety, JVM signal
conflicts, a Node thread that never terminates, `dlclose` hanging — those are
true for a Go-cored library and false here. Each one was re-measured against a
Go control rather than assumed away.

## What is prebuilt

| Target | Status |
|---|---|
| darwin/arm64 | **built and executed** — every number on this page was measured on it |
| linux/amd64 | the `.so` is built and the C smoke test runs on it in CI's `c abi` job; no language package has been run there |
| **linux/arm64** | **not built** |
| **darwin/amd64** | **not built** |
| **windows/amd64** | **does not exist — no DLL ships** |

The sidecar path has none of these constraints — it needs only the
`patala-sidecar` binary for your platform. But see the next line before planning
around that.

## The one thing that overrides every recommendation above

**The sidecar's rail registry is mock-only today.** `default_registry()`
registers exactly one rail, `"mock"`; any other `rail_id` gets a `404`. The
server, its auth, its error mapping and all six endpoints are real and exercised
over a real socket — but **direct mode is the only path to a real rail right
now**, whatever a package's default says. [Status](status.md) tracks it.
